name: Medical Vision-Language Benchmark
description: With the availability of large-scale, comprehensive, and general-purpose vision-language (VL) datasets such as MSCOCO, vision-language pre-training (VLP) has become an active area of research and proven to be effective for various VL tasks such as visual-question answering. However, studies on VLP in the medical domain have so far been scanty. To provide a comprehensive perspective on VLP for medical VL tasks, we conduct a thorough experimental analysis to study key factors that may affect the performance of VLP with a unified vision-language Transformer. To allow making sound and quick pre-training decisions, we propose RadioGraphy Captions (RGC), a high-quality, multi-modality radiographic dataset containing 18,434 image-caption pairs collected from an open-access online database MedPix. RGC can be used as a pre-training dataset or a new benchmark for medical report generation and medical image-text retrieval. By utilizing RGC and other available datasets for pre-training, we develop several key insights that can guide future medical VLP research and new strong baselines for various medical VL tasks.
evaluation_method: BLEU / ROUGE / CIDEr for generation; Recall@K (retrieval) and retrieval MRR for retrieval; common to report multiple metrics per task
general_score_metric: BLEU (for report generation) and Recall@K / MRR (for retrieval)
typical_sota_score: BLEU: ~10–30; Recall@1: ~20–60% (varies by model and pretraining data)
reputation: A recent (2023) domain-specific benchmark and pre-training dataset (RGC) that has gained moderate attention as a radiography VL baseline in medical VLP research.
notes: Relatively small domain-specific dataset (18k images) compared with general VL corpora; risk of domain shift and limited diagnostic labels; evaluation mixes generation and retrieval metrics; potential contamination from models pretrained on overlapping medical corpora.
